trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going up, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1); going right, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,1) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
The line must go down: up is number 7, which comes later; around the edge to (3,5) is number 5, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (4,5), the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 4. So the line goes right.
I can't rule out right or down yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 4. So the line goes up.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (right from cell (4,2)) was wrong, so the line must go down.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
I can't rule out up or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
Going up, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (up from number 3) was wrong, so the line must go right.
Going right, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,5). So the line goes up.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,5). So the line goes right.
Cell (4,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes around the edge to (2,1).
The line must go right: up is number 11, which comes later.
Going up would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes right.
The line must go right: up is number 10, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 7 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 16/25 cells (64%).
Generation 2: fitness 16/25. The best line covers 17 cells, the first 16 of them still look solvable.
Generation 4: fitness 25/25. The best line covers 25 cells.
Generation 4: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Tried 96 futures: 100% survive going left (best covers 40%); up 100%; down 4%.
Jackpot! A future covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 25 cells x 25 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 1,423 variables and 3,871 clauses in 0.00 s (403 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
